challenge.better_approach: Looked at (a) raising the tester's 120 s default, which widens every proof's budget and hides slow ones; (b) passing --timeout in every walk script, my scratch fix, which leaves every other caller (every-other-proof runs, the Dell's walks) at 120 s. A per-proof declaration is the mechanism the tester already reads.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the run time grows with the live corpus (two teeth read every ticket and seal), so 900 s, 3.3x the measured hollow, is headroom rather than a fixed cap that holds forever.

answers.falsifier: RED if the proof declares no PROOF_TIMEOUT_S, or declares one not above the measured 270 s hollow run, or a `bin/cairn test` of it with no --timeout times out. Horizon: the next walk over a ticket whose PROVES names this proof seals and hollows on the default budget.

answers.how: Add PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 900 at module level in cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_proof_coverage.py, commented with the measured run time as the inspector's live-corpus proofs do (test_address_sieve.py:27), plus one self-reading tooth and this ticket's PROVES entry.
answers.traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured): a proof that never finishes yields no reading, and clearance refuses the ticket on hollow_evidence_absent. Law 9: a timeout is red, never green.
answers.what: The proof_coverage proof declares a PROOF_TIMEOUT_S over its measured run, so a run on the tester's default budget seals it instead of timing out.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-19 on akiendelllinux: 8e2018855b31's walk hollow at 00:12 timed out at the tester's 120 s default for a proof that declares no PROOF_TIMEOUT_S (cairn/devices/tester/cli.py:543), so clearance refused PROVED and kicked the ticket to FIXME; the walk's seal step timed out again at 00:32 ('1 proof · 0 green · 0 red · 1 timeout'). Two diagnostic runs under --timeout 1200 took 174 s and 166 s; the sealed hollow took 270 s.
Every default-budget caller times this proof out, not only a walk script; the fix belongs on the proof.
